requirement: A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It MUST also build the book with the combined coverage reports of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, including the coverage collected by these checks, and on a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it MUST deploy the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
rationale:
I found no gaps. The workflow, `book.toml` and the repository test cover each obligation.

**Triggers.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml#pair[on]` runs the workflow on pushes to `main` and on all pull requests.

**Checks.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml#pair[jobs]/pair[test-and-build]`:
- `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` runs through the `habeas` alias in `.cargo/config.toml`, after `cargo build --release --locked -p habeas`.
- `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace` runs as its own step.
- `mdbook test` runs as its own step.
- The `JavaScript tests` step runs `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`. It also runs `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs`. That extra file is harmless and does not stop the required command from running.

**Symposium smoke test.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml#pair[jobs]/pair[symposium-hook]` is a separate job. It runs `python3 tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`, and that script exists.

**Book build with coverage.**
- The `Build mdBook` step runs `mdbook build` after the coverage step, in the same job.
- `book.toml#table[preprocessor.habeas]` runs `cargo habeas mdbook`.
- The preprocessor populates the combined coverage view through `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate]`, which implements `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`. That requirement is cited here as context and not reassessed.
- The coverage collected earlier in the job is therefore included in the build.

**Deploy.**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml#pair[jobs]/pair[deploy]` is gated by `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`.
- It has `needs: [test-and-build, symposium-hook]`, so it runs only after every check job passes.
- The `book` directory is uploaded as the Pages artifact on a push, and `actions/deploy-pages@v4` deploys it.

**Site URL.** `book.toml#table[output.html]/pair[site-url]` sets `site-url = "/habeas-codicem/"`.

**Tests.** `tests/repository.rs#fn[ci_tests_pull_requests_and_main_then_deploys_the_book_from_main]` carries a `{test}` reference. It asserts the following:
- the trigger block;
- the presence and order of the node, coverage, doctest, `mdbook test`, `mdbook build` and upload steps;
- the upload path `book`;
- the symposium smoke-test job;
- the deploy condition, the `needs` list and the deploy action;
- `site-url`.

The test does not separately assert that the coverage reaches the built book. It does enforce that the coverage step runs before `mdbook build`, and the coverage-to-book behaviour is tested under `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.

I found no unspecified extra behaviour that would count as a gap.

A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It MUST also build the book with the combined coverage reports of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, including the coverage collected by these checks, and on a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it MUST deploy the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
:::{req} run
`habeas coverage [-- <nextest arguments>]` MUST run LLVM-instrumented Rust tests
through `cargo nextest run`, forwarding the supplied arguments and preserving
nextest's configured test concurrency, filtering, and retries. With no supplied
arguments it MUST select the workspace.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
